 New proposed cuts to SNAP could impact millions of Americans if approved by the USDA (Spectrum News 1/Mason Brighton) 
 Proposed SNAP change could affect Kentucky families
 BY 
 Mason Brighton 
 Kentucky 
 UPDATED 4:40 PM ET Nov. 13, 2026 
 PUBLISHED 3:59 PM ET Nov. 13, 2026 
 PUBLISHED 3:59 PM EST Nov. 13, 2026 
 SHARE 
 LOUISVILLE, Ky. — The U.S. Department of Agriculture is proposing changes to SNAP eligibility that could cut food assistance for millions of people, including Kentuckians and children who rely on the program.
 This proposal would end one option for people to qualify for SNAP. The USDA estimates the change would cut benefits for 6.3 million people.
 The proposal comes as the number of people in Kentucky on SNAP has fallen by roughly 80,000 in the last year, according to state data.
 “We've been observing it and looking through it, reviewing it as best we can, based on the information that we have,” said Vincent James, CEO of the Dare to Care Food Bank.
 James said any disruption to SNAP benefits would affect families already struggling to make ends meet.
 Children would also be affected. Nationally, the USDA estimates 93,000 children would move from free to reduced-price school meals, and 28,000 would need to pay full price.
 Gov. Andy Beshear, D-Ky., addressed food needs in Kentucky on Thursday.
 “Far too many of our families are facing hunger and it's through no fault of their own,” Beshear said. “Prices have skyrocketed due to unlawful tariffs and Trump's war of choice. Plus his cuts to SNAP, which appear they're going to get even worse.”
 Dare to Care reports more people are turning to its partners for help, while the amount of federal support it receives is falling.
 Asked what he wants to see happen with the proposal, James said he wants the changes reconsidered.
 If approved, the USDA rule change would go into effect in 2029. The agency is taking comments on the proposal. Comments can be submitted electronically or by mail and will be considered if submitted by Dec. 10.
